title: Khufu cartouche allegedly painted by Vyse

tellings.quote: This is like this 1800's explorer. I forgot his name like Voss or Vas something. And he was hired by uh the British Museum. He was running out of funding. He was running out of time. Lo and behold, he suddenly finds the signatures of Kufu written in very suspicious ochre.

plain: The name of the pharaoh Khufu, painted inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt in a cartouche (an oval frame around a royal name), may have been painted there in the 1830s by Howard Vyse, the explorer who said he found it. Jay Anderson, a guest who calls himself a witness on other matters, tells this without naming a source and cannot quite remember the name ("Voss or Vas something"). He says the explorer was working for the British Museum, was running out of money and time, and then "suddenly finds the signatures of Kufu written in very suspicious ochre." If true, the main evidence that the pyramid belongs to Khufu would be in doubt.
